title: Un'Goro Crater
body: Un'Goro Crater is a vast sunken jungle in southern Kalimdor, ringed by cliffs, with the deserts of Tanaris to the east and the wastes of Silithus beyond its northwestern ridge. Steam rises from its pools, and at its heart the volcano of Fire Plume Ridge still smolders. Visitors say that entering it is like stepping into another world. The crater seems untouched by outside hands, and its creatures are nobler, mightier kin of beasts known elsewhere: devilsaurs and stegodons crash through the trees, ravasaurs hunt the marshes, pterrordax wheel overhead and great apes rule the northeast. Even the plants fight back, for the bloodpetals walk and lash at travelers. Stranger things lie hidden. Colored power crystals glitter across the basin, and crystal pylons of legend stand in remote corners. In the south the Gorishi silithid have dug a hive, and scholars wonder whether the silithid draw their strength from here. Most visitors shelter at Marshal's Refuge, a camp of stranded explorers in the north.

parts.body: On the northern bluffs above Marshal's Refuge stand a great stone terrace and a waygate, both tied to the titans. The waygate joins the crater to Sholazar Basin in far Northrend, and cultists of the Scourge now hold the terrace and the silent stone colossus that stands upon it.

title: Marshal's Refuge
body: Marshal's Refuge is a camp on high ground at the northern edge of the crater, where Marshal Expeditions fled when the beasts overran its base camps. It has become a home for the lost and stranded, where some arrive with a purpose and others by accident. A gnome with no memory lingers among the tents, two travelers who refuse to speak to each other sulk amid scurrying bloodpetal pests, and a castaway named Shizzle, too frightened of gryphons to fly home, builds a flying machine. J.D. Collie studies crystals in a nearby cave, the kodo Dadanga hopes for a snack of bloodpetal sprouts, and Gadgetzan bruisers guard the town's interests. Words written on a stone warn simply: beware of pterrordax.

title: Lakkari Tar Pits
body: Just south of Marshal's Refuge lie the Lakkari Tar Pits, black pools of sticky tar. Creatures of living tar drag themselves out of the muck, from creepers and lurkers to hulking tar lords, while bloodpetal flayers root along the banks and pterrordax circle above. Tran'rek, a schemer in Gadgetzan, wants the tar these beasts carry rather than ordinary pitch, sure that the chlorophyll in their skin makes it uncommonly sticky. Near the pits stands the Northern Crystal Pylon, one of the three great pylons the crater's few residents whisper about. Here too, close to the refuge, the dwarf engineer Karna Remtravel has pitched her camp to marvel at the crater's wonders.

title: Fungal Rock
body: East of Marshal's Refuge, Fungal Rock is the lair of the great apes of Un'Goro, where gorillas, stompers and thunderers roam the slopes. The tauren hunter Torwa Pathfinder counts their pelts a fair test of strength, but the greater test waits in a cave at the edge of their land, home of the huge red ape he calls U'cha, in his eyes one of the Earth Mother's greatest sons, with arms as thick as tree trunks. Here the engineer Karna Remtravel lost her mechanical ape, A-Me 01, after an alpha male rushed up to greet it. The apes seem to have accepted the machine: one big thunderer keeps her company, never straying from her side.

title: Fire Plume Ridge
body: Fire Plume Ridge is the smoldering volcano at the heart of the crater, south of Marshal's Refuge. Living blazes and scorching elementals walk its burned slopes, and the lava lake at its summit is said to be hot enough to fuse thorium and bone. The inventor Krakle, camped by the Golakka springs, suspects that the volcano warms his pools and wants its hot spots measured. On the ridge dwells Blazerunner, a powerful fire elemental wrapped in an aura that the refuge's residents say none has penetrated; many who tried to face him were pushed from the rocky paths. The explorer Ringo went to explore these slopes too, and his friend Spraggle fears he has stayed too long.

parts.body: The ridge keeps a treasure in one of its caves. There lies the Golden Flame, an artifact of power more vast than anything Linken has known, and dangerous in the hands of one with an evil heart. Blazerunner guards it, and it was with the Flame that he raised the aura that makes him all but invincible.

title: Golakka Hot Springs
body: In the west of the crater, steaming pools and geysers make up the Golakka Hot Springs. The inventor Krakle camps on their shore, puzzling over where the heat comes from. Seeing how close the pools lie to Fire Plume Ridge, he suspects the volcano, though he is too scared of its fire elementals to take the readings himself and has built a thermometer for braver souls to carry. Pterrordax, diemetradons and stegodons come down to the water, and the Western Crystal Pylon stands nearby. A cheerful woman named Simone strolls these shores with her growling pet Precious, delighting in the beauty all around and urging everyone she meets to enjoy what life has to give.

parts.body: Krakle's thermometer settled the question, or nearly. Its readings showed a clear link between the heat of the volcano and the warmth of the springs, though he means to check his equations. One puzzle leads to another: he points the curious to his friend Donova Snowden, who stays by hot springs in Winterspring with no volcano anywhere near them.

Simone is not what she seems. When someone who has seen through her disguise challenges her, she laughs at the foolish request and accepts. Then the smiling stroller becomes Simone the Seductress, a demon, and her little Precious turns into Precious the Devourer, a demon beast at her side. She will have the duel on her own terms: if others pile in, the pair simply vanish.

title: Terror Run
body: Terror Run, in the southwest of the crater, earned its name honestly. Herds of stegodons, plated, spiked and thunderstomping, crash among the trees, elder diemetradons bask nearby and frenzied pterrordax wheel overhead, while a great beast called Gruff roams among them. Marshal Expeditions came here to dig for the bones of long-dead stegodons and diemetradons, only to find plenty of living ones as well, and their reluctant chief digger declared the name fantastic, and did not mean it as praise. Dinosaur bones still lie scattered across the ground, and some of the research equipment the expedition left behind when it fled can still be found here. Gorishi reavers and workers stray up from the hive to the east.

title: The Slithering Scar
body: The Slithering Scar is a great silithid hive gouged into the south of the crater, the home of the insects called the Gorishi. Workers, wasps, stingers, tunnelers and reavers swarm through its tunnels, and the ore in its walls comes smeared with ooze. Deep inside lie larval hatcheries hung with dangling spawn, and a brood mother called Clutchmother Zavas prowls the hive. Hol'anyee Marshal finds the Gorishi entirely alien to the ecology of Un'Goro and wants to know why they are here at all.

title: The Marshlands
body: The Marshlands spread across the southeast of the crater, close to where the road from Tanaris comes down into the jungle. Hunters and runners stalk the reeds, venomhide ravasaurs carry a potent poison, and their nests lie scattered across the fen under the eye of a fearsome matriarch. Above them all is Lar'korwi, the dominant male whose name means sharp claw. At the southeastern edge of the marsh the ravasaur trainer Mor'vek keeps a lonely camp. The Eastern Crystal Pylon stands in these wetlands, and on the shore of a small pond lies a wrecked raft, though it is hard to see how so little water could ever have carried it.

title: The Shaper's Terrace
body: High on the bluffs above Marshal's Refuge lies the Shaper's Terrace, a great expanse of stonework tied to the titans. Beside it stands a titan waygate that joins Un'Goro to Sholazar Basin, far away in Northrend. On the terrace looms the Etymidian, a stone colossus made by the titans, silent and inert, with an empty rune-shaped slot in its chest. It is not alone. Death's Hand acolytes of the Cult of the Damned have taken the terrace, and their leader, High Cultist Herenn, keeps to the overlook nearby.

With the Omega Rune set into the empty slot, the colossus stirs at last and speaks: Omega Rune deployed, activation successful. Whatever it was woken for lies beyond the waygate, in the far north.

title: Linken
body: Linken is a gnome who turned up in Un'Goro with no idea how he got there. He remembers traveling, and a raft, and little else. The refugees find him friendly and a little strange: unlike most gnomes he shows no interest in gadgets or experiments, and he sometimes greets people with a demand for payment before catching himself. Asked how he came to the crater, he can only say that it is a secret to everybody. All he is sure of is that he came here for something important.

parts.body: At last his memory returns. Linken came to Un'Goro to fight the fire elemental Blazerunner, keeper of the Golden Flame, and that fight was to end a long journey. Yet he says he is no longer the hero. The hero is whoever brought his memory back, who must now finish what he began, and he warns that it is no task to attempt alone.

parts.body: With Blazerunner beaten, Linken sends the Golden Flame back to his homeland, where it will be protected and never again used for evil. He is deeply grateful to the one who did it, for without that help, he says, he would still have no idea who he is.

title: J.D. Collie
body: J.D. Collie is a gnome who has made a cave at Marshal's Refuge her home, though she cannot say how she came to the crater. She spends her days on the colored power crystals that lie all over Un'Goro, certain they hold a power everyone else ignores. Her experiments rarely go to plan. Many end in a yelp of pain and a promise that the last thirteen tries were only practice, and now and then she wonders aloud whether she should go back downstream. She admits she will believe almost anything she is told, including tales of great crystal pylons in the wilds. Linken remembers that she was kind to him when he first stumbled in.

parts.body: Her persistence pays off in the end. Once all three pylons have been found, J.D. works through her calculations and declares that she has finally figured it out. She sets down how the crystals and the pylons work in a manual, and gladly answers any question about them.

title: Williden and Hol'anyee Marshal
body: Williden Marshal and his sister Hol'anyee lead Marshal Expeditions, a troupe of scientists and explorers aligned with no faction who travel Azeroth in search of its wild and untamed majesty. Williden is the leader, still able to welcome a stranger warmly in the middle of disaster. Hol'anyee is the chief scientist and biologist, who holds that a setback is no reason for research to stop. Un'Goro was meant to be their greatest venture, and it has become their worst. They underestimated the savagery of the crater, lost their camps and most of what they brought, and now wait out their troubles at the refuge, while their chief digger offers his gold teeth to anyone who will carry him away.

title: Torwa Pathfinder
body: Torwa Pathfinder is a tauren hunter who camps where the road from Tanaris enters the crater. To him Un'Goro cries of the Earth Mother: its creatures seem nobler versions of the beasts of his homeland, and he thanks the spirits of every one that falls. He measures others not by race or calling but by the testing of spirit and mind against nature, and he respects any who can stand against the crater's great beasts. The ravasaur Lar'korwi killed his brother not far from his camp. Torwa has also sought druids for a gentler purpose, a toxin of bloodcap, Gorishi stings and Un'Goro soil to calm the devilsaurs, since killing one only lets another take its territory.

title: Karna Remtravel
body: Karna Remtravel is a dwarf engineer camped near Marshal's Refuge who finds the crater simply amazing, though not quite as amazing as the things she can build. Like her uncle Remtravel, who loves old places, she dreams of discovering new things from lost cultures. To study the apes up close she built a mechanical ape, A-Me 01, with scrying gems for eyes so that Karna could see all she saw. A-Me reached Fungal Rock before the link failed, the last image an alpha male rushing up to say hello.
sources: npc_text 2734 (amazing, engineering, uncle Remtravel loves old stuff, lost cultures)
quest 4244 description and reward text (mithril casing burnt out)

'Her uncle Remtravel' only, so darkshore.json's Prospector Remtravel is not retold.

parts.body: A-Me 01 stands at the edge of the apes' land, two huge dents in her shoulder and head and no power running through her. A panel on her back slides open on plain instructions: replace the mithril casing, then turn her off and on again.

The old mithril casing had burnt out. With a new one in place and the switch flipped off and on, A-Me woke and picked her way home, murmuring that A-Me is good, and Karna welcomed her back, promising to see to all those dents.

title: Spraggle Frock and Ringo
body: Spraggle Frock greets newcomers to Marshal's Refuge with the thought that some arrive with a purpose and some by accident, but everyone there has a story. Hers is one of fright. She never worried about the crater's beasts until she found the words 'beware of pterrordax' written on a large stone, and now she will not leave the refuge until someone thins their numbers. Her friend Ringo is bolder, or less careful. He set out to explore the volcano to the south and has been gone far too long, and Spraggle offers her canteen to anyone who will look for him, sure that he will need it.
notes: Converted: Ringo's fainting and the canteen's use (found on 4492, told in 4491) moved to part 2 on QUEST_ACCEPT 4491; his return to part 3 on QUEST_DONE 4491; Spraggle's relief over the pterrordax added as part 1 on QUEST_DONE 4501. npc_text 3546 and creature_text 9997, 9999 reread: classic. Earlier: Fact-check: verified. Spraggle female per display 11389 (Gender 1) and wiki (goblin; race left unstated). Ringo male (display 9340).

parts.body: Spraggle's fear eases a little once the frenzied pterrordax are thinned. She is still absolutely terrified of the beasts, she admits, but with fewer of them about she might feel safe enough to venture out of Marshal's Refuge at last.

Ringo is found on the slopes of Fire Plume Ridge, overcome by the heat and sure he is suffering from heat exhaustion. He thinks he can follow a guide back to the refuge, though he may faint again on the way, and a splash of water from Spraggle's canteen should bring him round.

Ringo made it back, soaked and unsteady but alive, and greeted Spraggle as one who had not expected to see her again. She has him home not in the best of shape, but in one piece, and is glad of whoever brought him.

title: Mor'vek
body: Mor'vek is a ravasaur trainer who keeps a lonely camp at the southeastern edge of the Marshlands, not far from where the road from Tanaris enters the crater. Around him hunt the ravasaurs of Un'Goro, kin of the raptors of the Barrens, clever and volatile beasts said to keep a code of their own. Among them are the venomhides, whose bite carries a potent poison.
sources: npc_text 2835 (Torwa: ravasaurs related to the raptors of the Barrens, intelligent, volatile, a code of conduct)
DB: Mor'vek 11701 at map 71.2,73.7, Torwa 9619 at 71.6,75.9
quest 13887 description and reward text (lighter colored shells; fewer with each clutch)
quest 13906 description and reward text (baby teeth, few have the dedication)
notes: Converted: the venomhide mount training (quests 13850, 13887, 13906, patch 3.2.0; mod-individual-progression does not gate them, and they are open from level 48) moved to parts 1-3 with minState 13 on QUEST_ACCEPT 13850, QUEST_DONE 13887 and QUEST_DONE 13906. Mor'vek (11701) and his title are older, so the opening keeps him as a ravasaur trainer among the venomhides, true in every era; his gossip (npc_text 14474, dedication) shows in every state and is kept. Earlier: Fact-check: Mor'vek's tolerance comes from poisoned blood (13850), not venom. Faction 2 confirmed: template 126 has EnemyGroup 2 (hostile to the Alliance), 13850 AllowableRaces 690. Check: his gossip line (npc_text 14474, menu 10438, patch 3.2.0) moved out of the opening into new part 1, minState 13, no triggers, so classic and Burning Crusade readers do not see 3.2.0 text; old parts 1-3 renumbered 2-4. Mor'vek is a vanilla NPC (wiki: removed 2.0.1, returned 3.2.0) and the module does not gate him, 13850-13906 or the venomhides.

parts.body: Mor'vek now sells venomhides as mounts to those who can earn one, and he warns every visitor that it takes a great deal of dedication to train and ride such a beast.

It is not a trade for the impatient. The beasts are poison through and through, in blood, spit and skin, and anyone who climbs onto one unprepared falls off dead within hours. He sells only to one who has built up a tolerance by being splashed with their poisoned blood again and again.

A tolerance is only the start. The rider must find the rare light-shelled eggs in the marsh nests, which grow fewer with every clutch, and raise the hatchling under Mor'vek's guidance, for venomhides are vicious and must be trained from the moment they hatch.

The hatchling must be hand-fed until it has shed all its baby teeth. Then Mor'vek fits the saddle and trains it to answer a whistle. Few have the dedication to hand-feed and raise a venomhide, he says, but they are well worth the effort.

title: Blazerunner
body: Blazerunner is a great fire elemental who dwells on Fire Plume Ridge, the smoldering volcano in the charred center of Un'Goro Crater. Living blazes and scorching elementals walk the burned slopes around him, but he is far stronger than any of them, wrapped in a fiery aura of his own, and those who close with him on the rocky paths of the ridge are met with bursts of searing flame.
sources: zone_areas area 537: Living Blaze, Scorching Elemental, Blazerunner 9376
smart_scripts 9376 (Blazerunner's Aura on reset, Blast Wave within 10 yards)
quest 4084 description (evil of the purest form, aura none can dispel)
quest 4005 description and reward text (charred center, aura, pushed from the rocky paths; totem to fight Blazerunner)
quest 3962 description and completion text (guards the Golden Flame, aura created using it)
notes: Converted: the opening is now only what a bystander at the KILL 9376 trigger sees (a fire elemental on the ridge, his aura, his blasts of flame). Eridan's verdict moved to part 1 on QUEST_ACCEPT 4084; the totem and the refuge's caution to part 2 on QUEST_DONE 4005; the Golden Flame and Linken's journey to part 3 on QUEST_ACCEPT 3962. Earlier: Fact-check: 'his strength comes from the Golden Flame' overstated; 3962 says only that he guards it and made his aura with it. Faction 0: template 91 EnemyGroup 1, hostile and killable for both. Check: 'burns fiercer' softened to 'far stronger' (elite, 'a strong elemental' in 4005); Blast Wave holds with and without the module (core: within 10 yards; module zone_ungoro.sql: in combat). Parts 1-3 reworded so they no longer repeat 49019 parts 2-3 (ACCEPT 4084, DONE 4005), 49004's opening and 49004/49010 part 1 (ACCEPT 3962) word for word.

parts.body: The druid Eridan Bluewind of the Emerald Circle names Blazerunner the purest evil. No one can dispel the aura that shields him, she warns, unless they hold power enough for the task, and she can teach how such power is gained.

That power is the Silver Totem of Aquementas, forged by the summoned elemental Aquementas from claws and an irontree's heart gathered in Felwood, and made to fight Blazerunner. J.D. Collie admits that everyone at the refuge gives him a wide berth: his aura has never been broken, and many who challenged him were thrown down from the ridge's paths.
sources: quest 3962 completion text (only the Silver Totem of Aquementas can remove it)

parts.body: Blazerunner is more than a wild flame. In a cave on the ridge he keeps the Golden Flame, a relic of immense power, and it was by its power that he made the aura around him. The gnome Linken's long journey was meant to end in a fight with him.

title: It's a Secret to Everybody
body: On the shore of a small pond in the Marshlands lies a wrecked raft. The pond seems far too small to have carried it, though a look at the trees around it suggests the water has not always stood at the same level. Whoever rode the raft is nowhere to be seen, and a little exploring in and around the water may turn up a clue to who it was. A few stray travelers have gathered at Marshal's Refuge to the north, and one of them may know more.
sources: feralas.json 35714 (Miblon guards the evoroot) and 35713 (Gregan, no triggers)
notes: Converted: the opening is the raft and the pond (3844). Parts on the steps where each is revealed: 1 the pack, Linken and the sword (QUEST_ACCEPT 3908, which follows the 3845 turn-in); 2 Donova and Gregan (QUEST_ACCEPT 3909); 3 the elixir and Gaeriyan (QUEST_ACCEPT 3912, which needs the elixir from 4041); 4 the gravestone and the flash of light (QUEST_ACCEPT 3914); 5 Linken's delight (QUEST_DONE 3914). Gregan's 4041 is auto-complete and told without a trigger. Earlier: Fact-check: Gaeriyan waits in a rocky crevice of the mountains due north (3912), not 'rocky hills'. Gregan's 4041 told without a trigger; feralas.json only mentions him.

parts.body: At the bottom of the pond lies a water-logged pack, and its contents lead to Linken at Marshal's Refuge, a gnome who finds them familiar, kind of. One memory stirs: his sword was meant to be strengthened, though he cannot say why. He sends it to Donova Snowden, who can temper it by the hot springs of Winterspring.

Donova tempers the blade, and learns with alarm that Linken has lost his memory, for he is not usually one to forget things. The sword is still not complete. One being can finish it, but speaking with him will be difficult: it needs a Videre Elixir, and only Gregan Brewspewer, camped in the wilds of Feralas, knows how to make one.

Gregan brews the elixir from evoroot. Whoever drinks it in the graveyard outside Gadgetzan passes into another form, able to speak with one the living would not normally even see, and walks due north to the mountains, where Gaeriyan waits in one of the rocky crevices.

Gaeriyan, who has had no visitor in a long time, tells of a gravestone in the graveyard unlike the others. Pushed firmly, it slides aside to reveal a small hollow that fits Linken's sword perfectly, and when the blade is laid there it is transformed in a strong flash of light.

Linken is delighted to have his sword back, finished at last, and he half remembers the one who brought it. Yet he still cannot remember why he needed it, and pays his helper for the work all the same.

title: The Golden Flame
body: Linken has his sword back, but not his memory. He knows he came to Un'Goro for something important, and he wonders whether he let it slip when he first arrived, disoriented, at Marshal's Refuge. The gnome J.D. Collie was very kind to him then, so he sends a helper to ask her in her cave at the refuge, with a warning to be careful: she is always messing with those crazy glowing crystals, and no one is quite sure what she is up to in there.
sources: felwood.json 36119 (Eridan Bluewind, Un'Goro quests mentioned without triggers)
notes: Converted: the opening is Linken's request (3941). Parts: 1 J.D.'s memory of the mumbling (QUEST_ACCEPT 3942); 2 Eridan and Blazerunner (QUEST_ACCEPT 4084); 3 the Book of Aquor and the totem (QUEST_DONE 4005); 4 Linken remembers (QUEST_ACCEPT 3962, which follows 3961); 5 Blazerunner falls and the Flame goes home (QUEST_DONE 3962). 4084 and 4005 are given in Felwood but filed under Un'Goro (QuestSortID 490); felwood.json leaves them to Un'Goro. Earlier: Fact-check: verified. Felwood's Eridan entry (36119) is not retold; this tells only the Linken chain. Check: part 5's closing reworded so it no longer repeats 49010 part 2 (both DONE 3962).

parts.body: J.D. remembers. Linken mumbled all kinds of strange things when he first arrived, likely after a hard bump on the head, but one stuck with her: he was making some sort of totem, and had to speak with someone named Eridan Bluewind in Felwood.

Eridan does not know Linken, but she knows what he sought. In the heart of Un'Goro dwells an elemental called Blazerunner, evil of the purest form, behind an aura none can dispel save those with the power to do so. That power she can teach, in return for silvery claws and the heart of an irontree from the creatures of Felwood.

For the claws and the heart, Eridan gives over the Book of Aquor, to be read from a circle of stones on the eastern point of Lost Rigger Cove in Tanaris. The elemental Aquementas is not pleased to be woken, but within the circle it forges the Silver Totem of Aquementas, and J.D. knows at once the elemental it was made to fight.
sources: quest 4005 description, log text and reward text

parts.body: All this time, J.D. realizes, Linken came to rid them of Blazerunner. The totem brings back the last of his memory. This was to be the final step of his journey, yet he declares that the hero now is the one who helped him. Blazerunner guards the Golden Flame, a power vaster than any Linken has known, and it is dangerous to go alone.

With the totem, Blazerunner's aura is stripped away and the elemental falls. The Golden Flame is taken from its cave, and Linken sends it home to his homeland to be guarded, never again to be used for evil, and he thanks his helper warmly for giving him back his past.
sources: quest 3962 log text, completion text and reward text

title: Marshal Expeditions
body: Marshal Expeditions came to Un'Goro on what was meant to be its greatest venture and met disaster after disaster. The crater's beasts overran its base camps in the southwest and the northeast, and the troupe fled for higher ground, leaving behind its food, its research equipment and even Williden Marshal's journal, later found mangled in the wilds. At the refuge, the expedition clings on. Williden needs the crate of foodstuffs and some of the equipment back if anyone is to survive. His sister Hol'anyee wants a scraping from the walls of the Gorishi hatcheries, to learn why the silithid are in the crater at all. Spark Nilminer, the reluctant chief digger, is meant to bring back bones of long-dead stegodons and diemetradons from Terror Run, though privately he admits that bones from living ones will do.
notes: Converted: the opening is the stranded expedition's three needs (3881-3884 descriptions); Dadanga's line dropped to fit the 140-word story opening (49001 keeps her). Parts on each turn-in: 1 supplies back (QUEST_DONE 3881), 2 Spark's bones (QUEST_DONE 3882), 3 Hol'anyee's sample (QUEST_DONE 3883). 3884 (journal returned) adds nothing beyond the opening. Earlier: Fact-check: verified.

parts.body: The crate of foodstuffs and the research equipment came back, and with them the expedition's hopes. Williden declares that the troupe has been saved, and its lives with it, and that they might now hold out in the crater for a while. Whoever brought the supplies home has a friend in Marshal Expeditions.

Spark got his bones, and with them gave a loud, pointed speech of thanks for digging them all out of the ground without hurting the native beasts in any way. Whether that is true he does not want to know, and he hands over a little something to keep the matter quiet.

Hol'anyee has her sample of the hive wall, and the expedition's research goes on. Stranded as she is in the middle of a savage land, she can give little in return, but she insists that none of the work done here would have been possible without the help she was given.

title: Crystals of Power
body: Power crystals of red, blue, yellow and green lie all over the crater, and most people ignore them. J.D. Collie does not. Certain they hold power, she experiments endlessly in her cave at Marshal's Refuge, so far without success, and sends out collectors when her supply runs low. She has also heard rumors of mysterious pylons standing in the wilds, large and lined with crystals inside, one somewhere in the north, one in the east and one in the west. Call her gullible, she says, but she is sure the stories are true, and that the pylons have something to do with the crystals.
notes: Converted: the opening is J.D.'s search and the rumors (4284 to 4288 descriptions). Parts: 1 the three pylons found (QUEST_ACCEPT 4321, which needs 4285, 4287 and 4288 done: their NextQuestID 4321 with ExclusiveGroup -4285); 2 the charms and the manual (QUEST_DONE 4321). npc_text 2810, 2834-2837, 2933 reread: classic. Earlier: Fact-check: verified. 4285, 4287, 4288 need 4284 (PrevQuestID), so 4284 is the only entry.

parts.body: The stories are true. Searchers find all three: the northern pylon close to the tar pits, the eastern in the Marshlands and the western near the Golakka springs. To the crater's few residents they are a mystery and a source of legend, with much speculation about their purpose, and J.D. sets to work on her calculations.
sources: quest 4321 description (needs all three pylon quests)

parts.body: From what is learned, J.D. works out how each pylon fuses two colors of crystal into one charm. One heals, one steadies the spirit, one hardens the body against blows, one weakens a foe's defenses, one bursts in a stunning blast and one raises a shield that strikes back at attackers. She sets it all down in a manual for those who would use them.

title: Torwa's Trials
body: Torwa Pathfinder grants his respect only to those who prove themselves against the crater's greatest beasts. The first test lies north among the great apes, whose pelts will clothe his tribe. The hardest is Lar'korwi, dominant male of the ravasaurs, whose name means sharp claw. Long ago Torwa's brother took meat from one of its kills. The beast followed him for days, destroying everything he touched, and when he fled the crater it killed him not far from Torwa's camp. To provoke Lar'korwi, a hunter must repeat the offense and steal meat from its freshest kill.
notes: Converted: the opening is the two entry points (4289 apes, 4290 Lar'korwi's backstory). Parts on the turn-ins: 1 the apes and U'cha's introduction (QUEST_DONE 4289), 2 U'cha (QUEST_DONE 4301), 3 the threshadon and the glands (QUEST_DONE 4290), 4 Lar'korwi drawn out and his head (QUEST_DONE 4292). Earlier: Fact-check: verified. 4289 and 4290 have no prerequisites, both entry points.

parts.body: The apes fall, and Torwa gives praise to the Earth Mother and thanks their spirits, though he calls the challenge small beside Lar'korwi. He has seen another test among the gorillas to the north: a huge ape in their cave that he calls U'cha, one of the Earth Mother's greatest sons.

U'cha was magnificent, huge and red, with teeth the size of daggers and arms as thick as tree trunks, a creature Torwa's people might go generations without seeing. Whoever bests him earns Torwa's word that the name of great hunter is deserved.
sources: quest 4301 description, completion and reward text

parts.body: The freshest kill turns out to be a threshadon, an odd find in this part of the crater, and Torwa keeps the meat for the confrontation to come. His final plan needs the scent glands of Lar'korwi's mates, taken where they guard their eggs west of his camp.

Laid together on a small trail into the mountains, among the bones of massive creatures, the meat and the glands draw Lar'korwi into the open. His head brings Torwa's highest praise: only the greatest of his ancestors, he says, could have done so much.

title: The Gorishi Hive Queen
body: Scholars in Darnassus and Orgrimmar suspect that the silithid draw their strength from Un'Goro Crater, and Alchemist Pestlezugg of Gadgetzan, who has already studied the bugs of Tanaris, thinks the idea worth testing. His research tells him the silithid are like bees: destroy a hive's queen, and the rest should be thrown into disarray. To bring the queen out he means to brew a lure, and for that he needs samples of the native Un'Goro soil and a scent gland taken undamaged from the Gorishi of the Slithering Scar, which is easier said than done.
sources: quests 4493, 4494 descriptions and reward texts (Gracina, Zilzibin; Pestlezugg: perhaps it is)
quest 4496 description, completion and reward text
notes: Converted: the opening is the plan (4496 description and request text); the lure and the crystal moved to part 1 on QUEST_ACCEPT 4507; the queen's death, the malign intelligence and Pestlezugg's unease to part 2 on QUEST_DONE 4507. The closing line about word going back to the scholars dropped: it rests on 4508/4509, whose turn-ins Darnassus (DONE 4508) and Orgrimmar own. The scholars' theory is kept to one clause, since darnassus.json 165710 part 2 tells Gracina's theory on ACCEPT 4493; tanaris.json 44030 parts tell the earlier analysis (DONE 82, 110) and are not repeated. Earlier: Fact-check: closing line about a stronger presence elsewhere (4510/4511) dropped, as darnassus.json's Gracina entry tells it; now ends with the word of the hunt going back to the scholars (4508/4509 turn-ins, unused). 4496 has no prerequisite (4493/4494 only lead to it), so it opens to both sides. 4508 unused.

parts.body: With his special additions the lure is ready. Somewhere in the hive's hatcheries, Pestlezugg believes, lies a crystal the silithid use as a hive-wide attunement device. The lure set upon it should roust out the Gorishi Hive Queen, though she will be protected by guards, and he wants her brain brought back for study, however icky that sounds.

The Gorishi Hive Queen falls, and her brain reaches Gadgetzan. Pestlezugg had come to believe that the silithid might be controlled by a malign intelligence, and he shudders to think what could command creatures so insidious. Even in victory he is uneasy: so clean a resolution, he warns, cannot be the full extent of their presence.

title: The Bloodpetal Feud
body: Larion and Muigin set out together and ended up lost in Un'Goro, and each blames the other. Larion says he knew the way until Muigin insisted on a shortcut; Muigin says he warned Larion they were going the wrong way. Now they camp a few steps apart at Marshal's Refuge, neither willing to speak first. Muigin has turned to mischief, sure that the wild bloodpetals of the crater could be trained to obey commands, if only he had samples to study. Larion, meanwhile, is plagued by plant pests night and day, and blames Muigin for every one of them.
sources: quests 4141, 4142, 4143, 4144 (Muigin, Alliance) and 4145, 4147, 4146, 4148 (Larion, Horde): descriptions, completion and reward texts
notes: Converted: the opening is the quarrel and the pests, true for both sides (4141, 4145 descriptions; pests 9157 visible in camp; npc_text 6741). Alliance parts: 1 Gregan's haze (QUEST_ACCEPT 4143, from Gregan), 2 Muigin's tamed sprouts and his confession (QUEST_DONE 4144, auto-complete). Horde parts: 3 Marvon away and Liv's zapper (QUEST_ACCEPT 4146, from Liv), 4 the zapper calibrated (QUEST_DONE 4148, auto-complete). Earlier: Fact-check: verified. 4141 AllowableRaces 1101 (Muigin, template 210 hostile to the Horde) and 4145 AllowableRaces 690 (Larion, template 106 hostile to the Alliance): one entry per side, faction 0. Check: part 3 no longer says 'the same' haze, since a Horde reader has not seen part 1. Triggers confirmed: 4143 (Gregan, QuestType 2) and 4146 (Liv, QuestType 2, QuestSortID 1417) are not auto-complete; 4144 and 4148 are QuestType 0, DONE only. Part 2 no longer has the sprouts running off and Muigin laughing: those are creature_text 9119 lines that nothing says (Muigin has no AI or script in the core or the module); it now rests on 4144's completion and reward text.

parts.body: Muigin found that the plants seem to have some small intelligence and sent one to his friend Gregan Brewspewer, an herbalist who left Ironforge for the quiet of the Feralas wilds and gets more visitors there than he ever did in the city. Gregan has never seen such plants, but he knows what will control them: Atal'ai haze from the sunken temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows.

Muigin admits he is vengeful. The haze goes into a heap of bloodpetal sprouts, plants not yet fully grown, and Muigin is sure the result will get Larion's attention. He even confesses that he knows the way home, but he will not leave until Larion admits that Muigin was right.

Larion spied on Muigin and caught him growing the pests, and he means to fight back rather than talk. His friend Marvon Rivetseeker of Ratchet is away studying the troll ruins of Tanaris, but Marvon's apprentice Liv Rizzlefix has built a short range bug zapper, fueled by Atal'ai haze from the sunken temple of Atal'Hakkar.

Calibrated with a bloodpetal sprout, the zapper is ready for Muigin's little friends. Larion insists the prank does not bother him at all, though he grumbles that if Muigin were not so stubborn, the two of them could already be on their way home.
